brief: UBS Sales & Trading commentary published 28-Oct-2026 ahead of Wednesday's FOMC decision. Markets price roughly 90% odds of a hold at 3.75-4.00%, and UBS economist Jonathan Pingle expects Chair Warsh to deliver a hawkish hold, keeping rate hikes in December and January as the base case; UBS frames gold and equity positioning around that event, noting equity sentiment stabilizing ahead of Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon earnings and neocloud credit spreads moderating, while flagging that weaker AI signals or renewed rates pressure could undermine the nascent rally. Separately, the RBNZ surprised markets by holding at 2.75% in a 4-3 vote, sending NZD down 1.5%, though UBS's NZ economist still expects hikes to a 3.25% terminal rate; Australia's hotter-than-expected Q3 CPI makes a November RBA hike very likely per UBS. UK Chancellor Healey's Wednesday Budget is expected to favor modest household relief over a fiscal reset, with shrinking fiscal headroom and reported bank-levy, surcharge-reversal and online-marketplace-tax measures. Other items: SK Hynix's KRW100trn shareholder payout, a US warning of possible Gulf strikes on Iran lifting oil, Israeli coalition deadlock, and an expected BoC hike Wednesday.
